chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Samāʿah, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: If you have discharged water and forgot to wash your private part until you performed salat, then you must repeat the wudu (ablution) and wash your private part.

So this report is to be understood as referring to the case where he had not performed wudu (ablution). But if he had performed wudu (ablution) and only forgot to wash the private part, then repeating the wudu (ablution) is not obligatory upon him; rather, only washing the area is obligatory upon him. And that which indicates this is what follows.

key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: the report or hadith being interpreted
key_terms.الْمَوْضِعِ: the place or affected area that must be washed
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing required for salat
key_terms.ذَكَرَكَ: your private part, the organ that must be washed in this context
key_terms.غَسْلُ: washing, specifically cleansing the relevant bodily area

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets to wash after discharge and performs salat, must they repeat their wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This report discusses a ruling related to ritual purity after discharge and the effect of forgetting to wash the private part before salat. It clarifies that repeating wudu (ablution) is required only if wudu (ablution) had not already been performed, while otherwise only washing the affected area is necessary.
